title: Cap. 6 Arg. 5 open: Useful ends that confirm application-grace by good pleasure
pass_a_gloss: Our opinion is confirmed from the most useful ends which it serves to illustrate, and which are plainly abolished by the contrary opinion. For example: If God, Christ's death having been granted, is nevertheless taken to distribute the grace by which it is applied, or not to distribute it to human beings according to his good pleasure, and not according to some disparity of human wills or actions.
pass_b_english: Our view is confirmed by the most useful ends it serves to bring out—ends the contrary view plainly abolishes. Take this case: grant Christ's death, and still take God as distributing or withholding the grace by which that death is applied to human beings according to his good pleasure, and not according to some difference among human wills or actions.
source_text: Confirmatur sententia nostra a finibus utilissimis quibus illustrandis inservit, quique per contrariam sententiam plane abrogantur. Verbi causa: Si Deus, Christi morte posita, sumatur tamen distribuere gratiam qua applicetur, vel non distribuere hominibus secundum beneplacitum suum, & non secundum disparitatem aliquam voluntatum aut actionum humanarum.
